items.title: Teletext fans rebuild Ceefax pages for modern screens
items.description: Hobbyists have released open tools that render classic 40 by 24 teletext pages in a browser. The projects draw on archived broadcasts and original character sets.

items.title: Chipmaker unveils low power processor for wearables
items.description: The new design promises two days of battery life in smart watches while adding on device speech recognition. Devices using the chip are due next spring.

items.title: Regulator opens inquiry into cloud storage contracts
items.description: Officials are examining whether long exit fees and data transfer charges limit competition. Providers say their pricing reflects real infrastructure costs.

items.title: Open source maintainers get new security funding
items.description: A consortium of companies has pledged money to audit widely used libraries. The first round will focus on tools for parsing and compression.

items.title: Researchers teach robots to fold laundry from video
items.description: A lab demonstrated a robot arm learning towel folding by watching human demonstrations. The team says generalising to other fabrics remains a challenge.

items.title: Satellite broadband launches in rural trial areas
items.description: Households in six remote regions have been given early access to a low orbit service. Early speeds average above 100Mbps with some evening slowdowns.

items.title: Browser makers agree shared standard for passkeys
items.description: The change should let users move passkeys between devices without relying on a single vendor. Support is expected in stable releases by the end of the year.

items.title: Museum puts 3D scans of its collection online
items.description: More than 5,000 objects can now be viewed and downloaded as models. Educators say the scans will help schools without access to the originals.

items.title: New battery recycling plant opens in the Midlands
items.description: The facility can process enough cells for 20,000 electric vehicles a year. Operators say recovered metals will go straight back into manufacturing.

items.title: Old modems sold as collectors items surge in price
items.description: Dial up hardware from the nineties is fetching surprising sums online. Sellers say buyers want the sounds as much as the equipment.
